findings.title: [P1] Restore message-listener deregistration in unmount()
findings.body: `unmount()` no longer removes the `"message"` listener. The handler is now registered anonymously (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`, line 14) and `unmount()` only does `this.socket = undefined` (line 18), so the closure — which retains `this` — stays registered on the socket with no way to remove it. Consequences under realistic use: (1) any message arriving after unmount still calls `render()` on an unmounted view; (2) the socket retains every unmounted view for its lifetime (memory leak); (3) repeated mount/unmount cycles accumulate listeners, causing duplicate renders and unbounded handler growth on a long-lived socket. This breaks the cleanup contract the previous code implemented and directly contradicts the PR's stated intent to preserve existing contracts. Fix: keep the stored handler (or use an `AbortSignal`/`once`-style teardown) and restore the `off("message", handler)` call in `unmount()`.
